The overall objective of the Pacific Regional Audit Initiative (PRAI) is to raise Pacific public auditing practices to uniformly-higher standards, which in turn is expected to improve transparency and accountability in managing and using public resources. Twenty two SAIs out of the 26 the Pacific Region SAIs will be the participants and beneficiaries of this initiative. It is intended that by end 2012, 80% of participating SAIs will be at level 3 on the PASAI capability model. The Pacific Regional Audit Initiative (PRAI) is a Pacific Plan initiative. The 26-member Pacific Association of Supreme Audit Institutions (PASAI) developed the PRAI design through an extensive two-year consultation process. In April 2008, the PASAI Congress held in Rarotonga, Cook Islands unanimously confirmed the PRAI design and the 2008 meeting of Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) Leaders endorsed the initiative. The success of this initiative will be measured by movements in relevant Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability (PEFA) performance indicators. Likewise, the project purpose is for public accounts of Pacific Island countries to be audited in a timely manner to uniformly-high standards, with enhanced audit impacts and improved audit capability. This will be measured by the timeliness of public accounts audits and the strengthening of Supreme Audit Institution (SAI) capacity as measured by the PASAI Capability Model. The activities supported by the IDF will contribute to a larger program for knowledge sharing and dissemination supported by ADB and otehr donors.
